chapters.title: Write an Orchard Core Recipe
chapters.subtitle: A JSON file that sets up and fills an Orchard Core site

steps.text: A recipe is a JSON file that sets up an Orchard Core site. It enables features, changes settings, and creates content types and content. In this video, you write one for a module, give it variables, and run it.

chapters.title: What a recipe is
chapters.subtitle: A file of steps, run in order

steps.text: A recipe is a file whose name ends in .recipe.json. Put it directly in the Recipes folder of a module or a theme, and Orchard Core finds it there. The module project embeds the file, so it needs no entry in the project file.

The file holds three kinds of content: properties that describe the recipe, variables, and a list of steps. Orchard Core runs the steps from the first to the last, and a step that fails stops the recipe.
Each step is an object with a name. The name picks the step, and the other properties are its settings. A step whose name no handler recognizes is skipped, so a misspelled name does nothing.
The first properties describe the recipe. The name identifies it, and other recipes use that name to run it. The displayName and the description are what the Recipes page lists.
Tags appear as badges next to the recipe, and the Recipes page leaves out a recipe tagged hidden. The author, the website, and the version are information about the recipe.
A recipe that sets issetuprecipe to true is offered on the setup screen, and the Recipes page leaves it out. Leave the property out of a recipe that you run on a site that already exists.
The file is read leniently: comments and trailing commas are allowed. Use a comment to explain a step where it appears.

chapters.title: Scripts and variables
chapters.subtitle: Compute a value once, use it in any step

steps.text: A script is a string in square brackets: a prefix, a colon, and the code. The prefix js runs JavaScript, and the prefix file reads a file. Any other prefix is not evaluated, and its brackets are removed.
Variables hold values that you define once and use in any step. Declare them in the variables object, before the steps, and read one in a script with the variables function.

Orchard Core evaluates a variable the first time a step reads it, and keeps the result. A variable that calls uuid gives one identifier to the whole recipe, so two steps can point at the same content item.
Scripts can read their surroundings too. The configuration function reads a tenant configuration key, with a default. The parameters function reads values such as AdminUsername and SiteName.

To keep long text out of the recipe, put it in a file beside it. A step reads the file with the file prefix and the text function, and the path is relative to the folder of the recipe. A variable cannot read a file.

chapters.title: Features, themes and settings
chapters.subtitle: The steps most recipes start with

steps.text: Start with the feature step. Its enable property lists the features to turn on, and its disable property lists the features to turn off. In a recipe run from Tools, Recipes, or during setup, the steps after it use what it enables.
A theme is a feature too, so enable it before you set it. The themes step sets the site theme and the admin theme, and a property that is missing or empty leaves that theme as it is.

The settings step changes site settings, such as SiteName, TimeZoneId, and HomeRoute. Any other property is stored under its own name, which is how a feature's settings, like the layer settings, are set.

chapters.title: Content types and content
chapters.subtitle: Define a type, then create an item

steps.text: The ContentDefinition step creates content types and parts. The BakeryPage type lists three parts: TitlePart, HtmlBodyPart, and a part of its own. PartName is the part, and Name is what the type calls it.
A part lists its fields. The BakeryPage part has one field, a text field named OpeningHours, with the display name Opening Hours.
If a type or part already exists, the step alters it. It adds the parts and fields you list, and merges their settings. A type's own settings merge only when the type has a DisplayName.

The content step creates content items from its data array. Each item names its ContentType, has a ContentItemId, and sets Latest and Published to true. Take the ContentItemId from a variable, and other steps can point at the item.
Each part's data sits under the part's name. TitlePart holds a Title, HtmlBodyPart holds Html, and a text field holds Text. Owner and Author come from the parameters function.
Tools, Recipes lists the recipes of the modules and themes, grouped by module. Let's search for Bakery. The Bakery Starter module holds our recipe, with its description and its tags.
Select Run, and confirm with Yes. Orchard Core runs the steps in order, from the feature step to the content step.
A notification reports that the recipe Bakery Pages has been run successfully. When a step fails, the notification names the recipe and lists the errors of that step instead.
The home page of the site shows the Bakery Page that the recipe created, with its title, its text from the file, and the opening hours.

chapters.title: More steps and reuse
chapters.subtitle: Other steps, other recipes, and migrations

steps.text: Other features add their own steps, such as Roles, Templates, and Layers. The documentation shows many of the built-in steps, each with an example.
The ReloadTenant step asks the tenant to reload, so that settings read only at startup, such as CORS policies, take effect. Place it after the steps that write those settings.
The recipes step runs other recipes by name. Each named recipe runs right after that step, before the next one, and a name that no recipe has is reported as an error.

A data migration can run a recipe as well. Inject the IRecipeMigrator, and call ExecuteAsync with the file name of a recipe kept in the Migrations folder of the module. Register the migration with AddDataMigration in the Startup class.

A data migration runs while the tenant is being activated. When a migration runs a recipe, the content step waits and imports its items after all migrations have completed. In a recipe that you run from Tools, Recipes, it imports them immediately.

That is a recipe: properties, variables, and steps that enable features, define content types, and create content, written in the Recipes folder of a module and run from Tools, Recipes. Thanks for watching.
